description.narrative: The project is implemented in the Philippines.The main outcome areas it contributes to are Equality and Worker's Rights, Democracy and Human Rights, Just transition and Gender equality. The main right holders are the members of the National Confederation of Transportworkers' Unions.Through conferences, trainings and leadership development the project aims to achieve that the NCTU and its affiliates are consolidated as democratic and sustainable unions capable of representing transport workers in all levels of decision-making areas.Project OrganisationsThe project is a cooperation between The National Confederation of Transportworkers' Unions NCTU and Swedish Municipal workers union (Kommunalarbetareförbundet).NCTU organises transport workers in the informal sector, mainly drivers and operators of mini-buses, public utility jeepneys, tricycles, pedicabs and other forms of public conveyances where employee-employer relationships are not present. Since NCTU was established in 2008, it has spread from its core areas Caloocan, Cavite, Batangas, Cebu, Iloilo, Davao, Cotabato, General Santos and Cagayan de Oro, and have started to reach other provinces like Bataan, Pangasinan, Mindoro, Iligan City, Dumaguete City, Mandaluyong City, Marinduque and Antique. NCTU has grown from 8.000 individual members in 2008, to 27.000 members in 2015. As of the end of 2018, the NCTU has 29 200 individual members of which at least 10 percent are dues-paying.Kommunalarbetareförbundet organises more than 14 000 bus drivers in Sweden, and has vast knowledge of union work in the field of public transportation. As such, it contributes with input and learnings from the Swedish context. It also has knowledge in organising workers in the informal sector through other international cooperation projects.Other Donors to the OrganisationThere is no information stated in the organisational description. NCTU has to add the information. (March 2022) The Friedrich Ebert Stiftung (FES) has financed the drafting of Operation Manual for transport cooperatives. This initiative was necessary to help the cooperative leaders to prepare themselves in managing the fleet and operation of their cooperative.Project ObjectiveTo strengthen social movement unionism in the transport sector as NCTU will increase its capacity to defend and advance the rights of workers.From 2020 to 2024, the project further intends to accomplish the following:1. Increase the representativeness of the NCTU by expanding in strategic areas.2. Improve the capacity of the NCTU to campaign for Just Transition.3. Develop NCTU's organisational capacity by genuine collective ownership and management of their jeepney fleets and consolidate all of NCTU's secondary cooperatives into a federation.Actor groupsThe main actors within actor group decision-makers" are various government agencies are the various government agencies like the Department of Transportation (DOTr), The Land Transportation Franchising and Regulatory Board (LTFRB), the Department of Labor and Employment (DOLE) and the Cooperative Development Authority (CDA).The main actors working in cooperation for this project are NCTU's labour center, SENTRO, the Labor Education and Research Network (LEARN), which supports the NCTU's efforts to develop its economic arm, and its allies abroad like the International Transport Federation (ITF).The main actors within actor group rightsholders are their trade union members.NCTU also mentions that within its' sphere of interest' are the transport drivers and operators and the commuting public. And within its immediate' sphere of control' are its leaders and the secretariat."
